name: TX-33
label: Safe D

key_factors: Colin Allred's large fundraising advantage and name recognition
Open seat with no incumbent on the ballot
model.rationale: The D+18 district fundamentals make this a Safe Democratic seat even without Crockett on the ballot, and Allred's $7.4 million war chest and statewide profile reinforce that. Markets price Democrats around 96%, consistent with a comfortable but open-seat margin.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending for Gillespie or an unusually strong Republican national environment could narrow the margin, though a flip remains very unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Jasmine Crockett (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Jasmine Crockett is leaving this Dallas-area seat to run for Senate, but the district remains solidly Democratic with an 18-point partisan lean. Former Rep. Colin Allred, who ran statewide in 2024, enters as the heavy favorite and has raised over $7.4 million, dwarfing the resources of Republican Patrick Gillespie, who reports little fundraising activity.

With no general-election polling available, the forecast rests on district fundamentals and prediction markets, which price Democrats near 96%. An open seat adds some uncertainty, but the underlying lean is strong enough that a Republican win would require a dramatic shift.
